## What the pinned code shows

**One SSRF sink, one reachable route.** `save_cover_from_url` does `requests.get(url, timeout=(10, 200))` with no scheme/host/address/redirect validation (`cps/helper.py:585-588`), and its only caller passes the caller-supplied `cover_url` form field straight in (`cps/editbooks.py:793-800`).

The only protection on the path is a role gate (`cps/editbooks.py:795-796`) plus a UI gate that also consults `config_uploading` (`cps/templates/book_edit.html:101`, `cps/admin.py:110`, `cps/config_sql.py:84`) — the server side only checks the role, not the stored config, unlike the sibling `/upload` route (`cps/editbooks.py:1026`).

**Traps recorded:** the unvalidated fetch (M4), redirect-following (M8), lexical-vs-resolved hostname check (M8), the role-only entry gate (M5), the provider-written cover URL (`get_meta.js:45`, `google.py:43`, `comicvine.py:55` → M6), and the `/static/generic_cover.jpg` cover-removal sentinel that a strict URL rule would break (M11).

## Verdict: not usable as a stacked task

Grouping by the shared-guard rule collapses everything to **one missing-protection group**: a single safe-fetch wrapper at `cps/helper.py:585-590` closes T1–T5, since the fetch has only one call site. All traps sit at distance 0-1, so the checkout does not hold the 3-5 independent places a stack needs. The other outbound-request sites (updater, LDAP, SMTP, Gmail `token_uri`) are admin-gated or fed by trusted APIs and would not be fair to test.

Two caveats I flagged in `unverified`: shell/git are disabled here, so I could not read the A-fix or B-fix diffs. I treated the `role_upload` gate at `editbooks.py:795-796` as the A-era fix (it is the only cover-URL guard in the tree, and the tree reports 0.6.16 Beta), but that identity is unconfirmed — which also means the `a_fix_leaves_b_open` answer rests on the in-tree code, not on the actual commit contents.
